articleSummary: Unknown pediatric illness with fever, skin rashes, anemia, dehydration, and kidney injury has killed at least seven children in Balaghat District, Madhya Pradesh, India, since late June. Affected areas include Adori, Machhurda, Bondari, and Kundeksa in the Birsa Tribal Development Block. The latest death was a 3-year-old named Priyanka Dhurve, who died Aug 9 after admission Aug 8; six other children (Lamanin Dhurve, 13; Sahil Dhurve, 1; Puja Dhurve, 1y9m; Sachin Markam, 5; Preeti Markam, 4; Arvind Dhurve, 4) died between June 26 and Aug 6 in Bondari and Kundeksa. Another death was reported Monday but not confirmed. Doctors from Jabalpur Medical College with pediatric specialists have examined patients; the cause remains unknown. Biological samples have been sent to a Pune lab; an AIIMS team from Delhi is visiting. Separately, Congress leader Digvijay Singh urged the Chief Minister, citing over 100 hospitalizations and 11 deaths in a week, and called for medical camps and financial relief for families.
notes: 原因不明の小児疾患クラスターで、発熱・発疹・貧血・脱水・腎障害を呈し、2026年6月末以降少なくとも7人の子供が死亡。プネーの研究所に検体送付、デリーのAIIMSチームが調査中。感染性か環境毒性かは未確定であり、続報とラボ結果の確認が必要。

articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri Province, Bunia) could surpass the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak. WHO reports over 4,300 infections and more than 2,000 deaths, with projections that deaths could exceed 11,000 if current trends persist, potentially peaking within six months and lasting up to 12 months. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a filovirus with no licensed vaccines or treatments yet; however, two therapeutic candidates and two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines have entered first-in-human trials, while existing vaccines are being evaluated for cross-protection. Transmission apparently began in February, with an official outbreak declaration on May 15. The crisis is worsened by unstable security, poor health infrastructure, wage arrears leading to strikes, and public distrust fueled by misinformation. A Nature Medicine study notes the virus is genetically distinct from past strains, arising from wildlife-to-human spillover rather than reactivation of earlier human cases. Cross-border concerns involve South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda.

articleHeadline: PKK Kota Tangerang optimalkan kader untuk putus rantai penularan TBC
articleSummary: TB in Tangerang City, Banten, Indonesia: Tangerang City PKK optimizes cadres down to the household level to break the tuberculosis transmission chain. The program promotes the Know, Find, Protect, Support until Cure approach, prioritizing early case finding, family protection, complete treatment, and stigma reduction. TB is airborne, spreading via coughing, sneezing, or loud talking, but not through handshakes, shared meals, or cleaned clothing. The Tangerang Dinkes has intensified TB control in the second quarter through initiatives such as Kelurahan Siaga TBC (TB Alert Villages), Ransel TB, and Active Case Finding (ACF) with X-ray. Self-screening reached 51% of its annual target by Q1 2026 and is accessible at https://ranseltbc.tangerangkota.go.id/ for all ages. If self-screening indicates a suspected TB case, the nearest puskesmas or confirmed facility will conduct direct screening (Mantoux and other tests) as needed.
notes: 地方自治体による結核対策啓発活動の通常業務報告であり、突発的なアウトブレイクではない。

articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating, potentially surpassing the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak. As of Aug 12, 2026, the outbreak has infected over 4,400 people and caused more than 2,000 deaths, with many fatalities occurring outside medical facilities, signaling unknown transmission chains. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo strain; there is no approved vaccine, though two vaccines have entered early-phase clinical trials. By contrast, the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak—centering in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone—had over 28,000 infections. This Congo outbreak has already become the largest in the country’s history, prompting urgent public health measures and investigations into infection sources and potential unidentified transmission routes.

articleSummary: Eight children in Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh, have died from a mysterious illness affecting Baiga tribal communities in Adori and Macharda Panchayats since 26 June. By 13 August the death toll reached eight: Lamanin and Sahil (Bondari siblings), Puja, Sachin, Kundeksa, Arvind (6 August), Mangli Markam (8 August), and three-year-old Priyanka Dhurve (admitted 9 August; died 11 August). Affected children showed pneumonia, anemia, dehydration, fever, itching, malaria, and kidney involvement. Samples have been sent to a Pune laboratory; results are pending. Investigations by Jabalpur Medical College and Balaghat doctors have not yet determined a cause. Civil Surgeon Dr. Nilay Jain confirmed all cases originate from Adori and Macharda villages. Former CM Digvijay Singh urged a statewide probe, accountability for officials, Rs 10 lakh per family in compensation, and airlifting to Nagpur, Raipur, or Bhopal hospitals with government funding.

articleSummary: COVID-19 variant PQ.16.1.1 has been detected in several countries and is being monitored by WHO; Indonesia has not detected it as of August 12, 2026. WHO data as of July 8, 2026 show 457 PQ.16.1.1 sequences reported to GISAID, from samples up to Epidemiological Week 25, across eight countries. The majority (438 sequences, 95.8%) originate from the Western Pacific Region, with Singapore contributing 388 sequences (84.9% of global sequences). Other reporting countries include Hong Kong SAR (34), Australia (10), United States (10), Canada (8), South Korea (5), France (1), and Taiwan, China (1). Kemenkes director-general Andi Saguni states there is currently no concern about widespread transmission in Indonesia; no import/export case reports are noted. Health authorities urge continued adherence to COVID-19 preventive measures and vigilance for respiratory symptoms, especially in crowded places.
notes: 記事の主題はインドネシア保健省の声明だが、実際の変異株検出はシンガポール・香港（中国）・オーストラリア・米国・カナダ・韓国・フランス・台湾で報告されている。対象国リストのうち香港（中国）のみ実際の症例報告あり。インドネシアでは未検出のため発生国として計上しない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Four consecutive people were admitted to the ICU due to tetanus! Even small wounds can cause big trouble!
articleHeadline: 连续4人因破伤风住进ICU！小伤口也可能惹上大麻烦！
articleSummary: Four consecutive tetanus patients were admitted to the ICU of Hunan Provincial People’s Hospital (Emergency Department) on August 12, 2026, after injuries with contaminated deep, narrow wounds (e.g., nails, wood splinters, soil) and inadequate wound care. All presented with generalized muscle spasms, trismus (jaw locking), neck stiffness, and respiratory failure, requiring artificial airway and mechanical ventilation. Treatment included tetanus immune globulin to neutralize free toxin, antibiotics, intensive sedation/analgesia, nutrition support, and complication prevention; all four improved to no longer be life-threatening. The report underscores prevention via prompt wound management and vaccination: thoroughly rinse and debride wounds, then assess tetanus risk in hospital; adults at high risk should complete primary immunization and receive boosters based on last dose (last <5 years: no booster; 5–10 years: one booster; ≥10 years: one booster). For incomplete histories, passive immunization may be considered. Incubation is 3–21 days; seek care for fatigue, jaw weakness, or muscle rigidity.
notes: 破傷風は感染症だが人から人へは伝染しないため、IHR/WPRO基準における流行可能性は該当しない。重症例(ICU入院)はあるが散発的な創傷管理不備によるもので、公衆衛生上の緊急対応は不要と判断。
